No withdrawal shall be made for Emergency Expenditures under Category (8), unless and until the Bank is satisfied, and notified theBorrower of its satisfaction, that all of the conditions established under Section III.B.1(e) of Schedule 2 to the Loan Agreementin respect of said expenditures have been met.

No withdrawal shall be made under Category (7) until the Environmental and Social Management Framework, the Indigenous PeoplesPlanning Framework, the Labor Management Procedures and the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (as defined in the Amendment Letter) havebeen updated by the Borrower in a manner satisfactory to the Bank, adopted and re-disclosed in country and in the Banks website.

No withdrawals shall be made under Category (6) and Category 7 until the PMU has updated the Operational Manual in a mannersatisfactory to the Bank for the provision of COVID-19 Emergency Response Grants.

Schedule 2-Section I, A.6. The Borrower, through MAG (through the PMU), shall, not later than nine (9) months after the EffectiveDate, establish, and thereafter operate and maintain, at all times during Project implementation, a computerized management andmonitoring information system, satisfactory to the Bank, for purposes of monitoring the execution of each Beneficiary under anInvestment Subproject.

Schedule 2-Section I. A. 3. For purposes of enabling INDI to provide the required assistance under the Project, including,inter-alia, for the carrying out of strategic capacity building activities and for the provision of support for the implementationof the ESCP, as applicable, the Borrower, through MAG, shall, not later than four (4) months after the Effective Date, enter intoan agreement with INDI (the INDI Participation Agreement), all under terms and conditions acceptable to the Bank and as set forthin the Operational Manual.

Schedule 2-Section I. B. 3. The Borrower, through MAG (through the PMU), shall furnish to the Bank for its prior review andapproval the proposed Investment Subprojects in accordance with the criteria set forth in the Operational Manual and the ESCP.

Schedule 2-Section I. B.1. Upon approval of the pertinent Investment Sub-project under Part 2 of the Project and prior to thecarrying out of said Investment Sub-project, the Borrower, through MAG (through the PMU), shall enter into a sub-project agreement(the Investment Sub-project Agreement) with the pertinent Investment Sub-project Beneficiary under terms/conditions acceptable tothe Bank.

Schedule 2-Section I. B.4. The Borrower, through MAG (through the PMU), shall refrain from presenting to the Bank Loan withdrawalapplications and/or withdrawing Loan proceeds from the Designated Account under Category (2) of Section III.A of Schedule 3 of theLoan Agreement to finance any given Investment Subproject, until the Borrower, through MAG (through the PMU), has furnished to theBank, evidence, acceptable to the Bank, indicating that the auditor to carry out the audits referred to in Part 3(b)(iii) of theProject has been hired as provided in Section I.A.5 of Schedule 2 of the Loan Agreement.

The PMU shall refrain from presenting to the Bank Loan withdrawal applications and/or withdrawing Loan proceeds from the DesignatedAccount under Categories (6) and (7) to finance any given COVID-19 Emergency Assistance Plans, until the Borrower has furnished tothe Bank, acceptable evidence indicating the auditor to carry out the audits referred to in Part 3(b)(iii) of the Project.

Upon approval of the pertinent COVID-19 Emergency Assistance Plan under Part 4 of the Project, and prior to the carrying out ofsaid Emergency Assistance Plan, the Borrower (through the PMU), shall enter into an agreement (the COVID-19 Emergency ResponseAgreement) with the pertinent COVID-19 Emergency Response Recipient under terms and conditions acceptable to the Bank.

title.narrative: Members of Beneficiary Organizations (Agricultural Producer Organizations and Indigenous Communities) participating in investment subprojects and adopting climate smart technologies or practices.

comment.narrative:
Description (indicator definition): It measures the number of PAO and CI members participating in the implementation of investment subprojects who carry out one or more climate-smart practices, understood as sustainable agricultural practices.

Scope: Total number of organized agricultural producers and indigenous community members participating in investment subprojects who carry out one or more climate-smart practices.

title.narrative: Increased gross value of sales (in real terms) by Beneficiary Organizations (Agricultural Producer Organizations and Indigenous Communities).

comment.narrative:
Investment subprojects under Component 2 have not concluded yet.
This indicator measures, in percentage terms, the increase in the gross value of annual sales of the beneficiary indigenous organizations and communities.
The gross value refers to the total income of each beneficiary organization (PAO and CI) derived from recorded sales during the period of one year from the implementation of the investment subproject.
Gross value of sales: this is the amount in guaranÃ­es resulting from the quantity sold multiplied by the unit price of the commercialized product. The following formula will be applied to each PAO and CI:
PDO Indicator 1 = ((gross value of sales in year t of the beneficiary organization) - (gross value of sales in year 0 of the beneficiary organization)) / (gross value of sales in year 0 of the beneficiary organization) * 100
The average of all PAO and CI will then be calculated.

title.narrative: Beneficiary Organizations (Agricultural Producer Organizations and Indigenous Communities) that continue to realize sales at project closing according to approved investment subproject.

comment.narrative:
Investment subprojects under Component 2 have not concluded yet.
This indicator measures, in percentage terms, the proportion of beneficiary PAOs and CIs with investment subprojects that continue to sell their agricultural products (resulting from the promoted value chain) at the close of the PIMA project. The following formula will be applied to each PAO and CI:
ODP Indicator 2 = (number of beneficiary organizations and CIs that continue to make sales at the close of the project) / (number of beneficiary organizations and CIs with investment subprojects) * 100
The average of all PAOs and CIs will then be calculated.

comment.narrative: The organizational and managerial capacity of each participating Beneficiary Organization (Agricultural Producer Organization or Indigenous Community) will be assess as a baseline point and throughout the implementation period to record its increased status, by using a multi layer composite index to be developed under the Project.

title.narrative: Agricultural Producer Organizations and Indigenous Communities benefiting from the project by implementing investments Subprojects.

comment.narrative:
Description (indicator definition): Quantification of PAO and CI organizations benefiting from the implementation of investment subprojects in the various windows enabled by the Project.
Scope: Total number of organizations implementing investment subprojects.
Method of information collection: Review of the Resolution approving investment subprojects.
Calculation formula: Sum of the number of PAO and CI organizations implementing investment subprojects.
Source of information: Summary of PAO and CI organizations benefiting from investment subprojects and the Project's Information Management and Monitoring System.
Means of verification: Resource Transfer Request, Project General Ledger, and Investment Subproject Monitoring Report.

title.narrative: Individuals directly benefiting from the project, disaggregated by gender and ethnicity.

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the number of individuals who directly benefit from the project, disaggregated by gender and ethnicity. Beneficiaries include those from Component 2 and Component 4, as well as recipients of technical assistance services and training provided under Component 1. According to the 2022 Population Census, the average household size is 3.5 members. For indigenous communities, the average household size is 5 family members. The abrupt change in the number of beneficiaries is due to previous reports not including family members. The calculation formula accounts for each agricultural producer and member of indigenous communities (disaggregated by gender and ethnicity) and multiplies by the corresponding coefficient.

title.narrative: Members of Agricultural Producer Organizations and Indigenous Communities receiving training and capacity building from the project

comment.narrative:
This indicator cumulatively measures the number of agricultural producers and CI members who receive training in various topics through the project. This indicator will be disaggregated by gender and by the number of young people aged 18 to 29.
The types of training promoted by the project include organizational strengthening, value chains and commercialization, project development and management, and environmental and social topics. It is calculated as the sum of the number of agricultural producers and CI members trained in various areas through the project, disaggregated by gender and distinguishing young people.
The report is cumulative, and necessary precautions are taken to avoid counting beneficiaries more than once.

title.narrative: Subproject "expressions of interest" submitted for review by Beneficiary Organizations (Agricultural Producer Organizations and Indigenous Communities) (Number)

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the number of potential Beneficiary Organizations presenting "expressions of interest" resulting from the calls for proposals. It is calculated as the sum of the expressions of interest submitted by PAOs and CIs. The report is cumulative.

title.narrative: Farmers reached with agricultural assets or services

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the number of farmers who were provided with agricultural assets or services as a result of World Bank project support. "Agriculture" or "Agricultural" includes: crops, livestock, capture fisheries, aquaculture, agroforestry, timber, and non-timber forest products. Assets include property, biological assets, and farm and processing equipment. Biological assets may include animal agriculture breeds (e.g., livestock, fisheries) and genetic material of livestock, crops, trees, and shrubs (including fiber and fuel crops). Services include research, extension, training, education, ICTs, inputs (e.g., fertilizers, pesticides, labor), production-related services (e.g., soil testing, animal health/veterinary services), phyto-sanitary and food safety services, agricltural marketing support services (e.g., price monitoring, export promotion), access to farm and post-harvest machinery and storage facilities, employment, irrigation and drainage, and finance. Farmers are people engaged in agricultural activities or members of a agriculture-related business (disaggregated by men and women) targeted by the project.

title.narrative: Agricultural Producer Organization and Indigenous Communities receiving services and assets from the project as response to Covid-19

comment.narrative:
Description (indicator definition): It measures the number of PAO and CI organizations implementing Emergency Assistance Plans in response to COVID-19.
Scope: Total number of Emergency Assistance Plans implemented by PAO and CI organizations in response to COVID-19.
Method of information collection: PAE documents, technical approval reports of the plans, and MAG Resolution approving plans for PAO and CI in response to COVID-19 until the end of 2022.
Calculation method: Sum of the number of PAO and CI organizations implementing emergency plans in the Eastern and Western Regions in response to COVID-19.
Source of information: Summary of PAO and CI organizations benefiting from PAE.
Means of verification: Resource Transfer Request, Project General Ledger, and PAE Follow-up Report.

title.narrative: Agricultural Producer Organizations and Indigenous Communities receiving services and assets from the project as response to Covid-19

comment.narrative: This indicator counts the number of Emergency Assistance Plans (PAE) funded for PAOs and CIs in the Eastern and Western Regions in response to Covid-19. This is the sum of the number of plans funded for PAOs and CIs in response to Covid-19.

title.narrative: Members of beneficiary Agricultural Producer Organizations and Indigenous Communities receiving services and assets as emergency response to Covid-19

comment.narrative:
Description (indicator definition): It measures the number of PAO and CI members who received non-reimbursable funding for the acquisition of goods and/or services in response to the COVID-19 emergency.
Scope: Total number of PAO and CI members benefiting from access to non-reimbursable funding for the acquisition of goods and/or services in response to COVID-19.
Method of information collection: List of members of PAO organizations and CI members benefiting from non-reimbursable funding for the acquisition of goods and/or services in response to COVID-19.
Calculation method: Sum of the number of PAO and CI members who received goods and services as an emergency response to COVID-19 in the Eastern and Western Regions of the country.
Source of information: Beneficiary database and summary of PAO and CI organizations benefiting from PAE.
Means of verification: List attached to the request submitted by the organizations and CI, and Annex 23 of the organizations' Accountability Report
